boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on campus-edge and downtown corridors within Florida State University’s practical Tallahassee orbit, each paired with one directly sourced reason.

cards.title: Order a Fresh-Made Pie
cards.subtitle: West Gaines Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow the West Gaines Street corridor to order pizza made with fresh ingredients and house-made components at the 603 W. Gaines location.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge pizza stop whose official page documents its from-scratch approach.
cards.evidence_claim: The business lists its Gaines Street location at 603 W. Gaines St. #3 and says it uses fresh ingredients and makes items such as meatballs and ranch in house.
cards.access_notes: Official hours currently list service from 11 a.m. until at least 1 a.m.; ordering food requires a purchase.

cards.title: Compare Dining and Shopping Options
cards.subtitle: West Madison Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the West Madison Street corridor and use CollegeTown as one pedestrian-oriented cluster for comparing dining and shopping choices.
cards.short_summary: A named mixed-use destination two blocks from campus with multiple storefront choices.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida State University describes CollegeTown as two blocks from campus and as a pedestrian-friendly place offering dining and shopping.
cards.access_notes: The district is at 805 W. Madison Street; individual tenants set their own hours and access conditions.

cards.title: View Color-Shifting Public Art
cards.subtitle: Gaines Street and Woodward Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Pause along the Gaines Street–Woodward Avenue corridor to view the glass sculpture from the sidewalk as its colors change with light and angle.
cards.short_summary: A large illuminated glass-and-metal artwork marks FSU’s southern campus edge.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU says Declaration is a glass, metal and light sculpture in the Gaines Street and Woodward Avenue roundabout whose panes change color with light and viewing angle.
cards.access_notes: Observe from legal pedestrian areas around the active roundabout; do not enter the traffic island.

cards.title: Check the Arena Event Calendar
cards.subtitle: West Pensacola Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the West Pensacola Street corridor to reach the arena, then check the official event listing before choosing a game, show, or gathering.
cards.short_summary: FSU’s nearby multipurpose arena hosts ticketed events in a clearly documented venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The official fan guide identifies Donald L. Tucker Civic Center at 505 W. Pensacola Street and documents arena guest services and event-dependent entry.
cards.source_title: Fan Guide A–Z | Donald L. Tucker Civic Center
cards.access_notes: Door times, admission and permitted items vary by event; consult the official event page before arriving.

cards.entity_name: LeRoy Collins Leon County Main Library
cards.title: Attend a Public Library Program
cards.subtitle: West Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Continue along the West Park Avenue corridor to use the Main Library’s public programming; confirm the selected event’s details before leaving.
cards.short_summary: The downtown county library provides a concrete off-campus setting for public talks and programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Leon County identifies the Main Library at 200 W. Park Avenue and lists public educational events there, including programs explicitly marked free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Program schedules and registration requirements vary; verify the county listing for the event you plan to attend.

cards.title: Choose a Planetarium or IMAX Program
cards.subtitle: South Duval Street corridor
cards.notes: Take the South Duval Street corridor to the center and compare current planetarium, IMAX, and space-science programs before selecting a show.
cards.short_summary: A downtown FAMU–FSU outreach facility turns a nearby block into a space-science outing.
cards.evidence_claim: The center identifies itself as the FAMU–FSU College of Engineering’s K–12 outreach facility and lists its address as 200 South Duval Street.
cards.source_title: Contact Us | Challenger Learning Center of Tallahassee
cards.access_notes: Showtimes, tickets and program eligibility vary; review the center’s current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Take a Self-Guided Capitol Tour
cards.subtitle: South Monroe Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow the South Monroe Street corridor to check in at the Rotunda desk and request the museum’s self-guided tour information.
cards.short_summary: The restored historic statehouse offers a free, structured introduction to Florida government history.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s official visitor page lists free admission, self-guided programs and its location at 400 South Monroe Street.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m., and Sunday noon–4:30 p.m.; holiday closures apply.

cards.title: Use the Public Observation Level
cards.subtitle: South Monroe Street and Apalachee Parkway corridor
cards.notes: Approach from the South Monroe Street–Apalachee Parkway corridor, clear security, and request self-guided visitor information inside.
cards.short_summary: The working state capitol is open to public visitors on weekdays without admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida’s Department of Management Services says the Capitol is at Monroe Street and Apalachee Parkway, is open to the public on weekdays and has free admission.
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; state holidays and security or legislative actions may alter access.

cards.title: See a Contemporary Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Railroad Square corridor
cards.notes: Follow the Railroad Square corridor to the nonprofit gallery and check its current exhibition page before planning an art-focused visit.
cards.short_summary: A former lumber warehouse now provides a dedicated contemporary-art destination near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: 621 Gallery describes itself as a nonprofit arts exhibition and programs space in a former 1940s lumber warehouse at Railroad Square Art Park.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists limited weekly gallery hours; verify the current schedule and exhibition status before traveling.

cards.title: Browse Vintage Records and Décor
cards.subtitle: Railroad Square corridor
cards.notes: Continue through the Railroad Square corridor to browse the shop’s documented mix of vintage clothing, records, furniture, art, and décor.
cards.short_summary: A named Railroad Square storefront offers a visually varied vintage-shopping stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Tallahassee lists The Other Side Vintage at 607 Railroad Square and documents its clothing, furniture, vinyl, jewelry, art and collectible inventory.
cards.source_title: The Other Side Vintage | Visit Tallahassee
cards.access_notes: Store hours and inventory can change; check the business’s linked official channel before making a dedicated trip.
